title: Add config/db migration for route quantization_profile_ref (backward compatible)
author: Michael Nguyen
release_notes: Adds backward-compatible persistence + serialization for route-level quantization_profile_ref. No behavior change unless feature flags are enabled.
body:
Summary: This PR introduces the database/config migration plumbing required to safely roll out the new route field `quantization_profile_ref` (see PR #18411) across environments with mixed-control-plane versions and cached route config. The changes are explicitly backward compatible: older binaries continue to read/write routes without the field, and newer binaries tolerate missing/unknown values. The migration is designed to support a staged rollout (dual-read/dual-write) and a fast rollback path, and it integrates with the global kill-switch introduced in ENG-5819.

Why: We need to persist per-route quantization settings without breaking existing route serialization or requiring a hard cutover. During rollout we will have (a) older Console/SDK clients, (b) mixed control-plane deployments, and (c) cached route config objects. We also need deterministic policy evaluation (no "default" surprises) and an auditable way to confirm what value is stored vs. resolved.

What’s included:
- DB migration adding a nullable `quantization_profile_ref` column to `route_configs` (and corresponding field in the config snapshot table) with no default.
- Backward-compatible serializer/deserializer for route config JSON/proto payloads: unknown field is ignored; missing field maps to `DEFAULT` semantics.
- Dual-write logic behind `ff.route_quant_profile_dual_write` (write both legacy route blob and the new column).
- Dual-read logic behind `ff.route_quant_profile_dual_read` (prefer new column when present, otherwise fall back to legacy route blob).
- Backfill job scaffold to copy the parsed value from legacy blob into the new column for existing routes (safe to run multiple times).
- Guardrails: invalid/empty refs normalize to `"default"` at the storage boundary; policy engine still enforces compatibility and may resolve to fallback at request time.
- Operational switches:
  - `ff.route_quant_profile_migration_enabled` (gates running the backfill task and enabling dual-* flags in prod)
  - integration with the existing global kill-switch so that even if stored refs exist, runtime resolution is forced to baseline when kill-switch is on.

Staged rollout plan (proposed):
1) Deploy this PR everywhere with all flags OFF. Verify no schema/serialization regressions.
2) Enable `ff.route_quant_profile_dual_write` in staging, then prod (writes new column for any route updates).
3) Run backfill in staging; validate row counts and sampling (see Runbook section below). Repeat in prod.
4) Enable `ff.route_quant_profile_dual_read` in staging (reads new column when present) and validate resolved quant_profile_id tagging in traces. Then enable in prod.
5) After 2 release trains with no issues, we can remove legacy parsing as a follow-up PR (not in scope here).

Runbook notes:
- Backfill job is idempotent and rate-limited. It emits metrics: `route_quant_profile_backfill_rows_total`, `route_quant_profile_backfill_rows_updated`, `route_quant_profile_backfill_parse_failures`.
- Rollback: disable dual_read first, then dual_write; no data loss (column remains but is ignored). If needed, disable via global kill-switch to guarantee baseline behavior.

Testing:
- Unit tests for JSON round-tripping with/without the field and with unknown enum values.
- Migration tests verifying column existence, nullability, and index creation.
- Integration test that simulates mixed versions: old writer -> new reader, new writer -> old reader.

Notes:
- This does not change request-time behavior by itself. Policy compatibility checks and runtime application remain gated by the route-level enablement and kill-switch paths.

Refs:
- Linked work: ENG-5814 (route config field), ENG-5815 (compat checks), ENG-5819 (kill-switch)
- Related PRs: #18411 (route config field), #18488 (kill-switch)

Checklist:
- [x] Backward-compatible schema change
- [x] Dual read/write behind flags
- [x] Backfill scaffold + metrics
- [x] Mixed-version tests
- [x] Release notes / rollout steps

conversation: 2025-03-17 Ethan Park (review): Can we guarantee older control-plane builds won’t choke on the new serialized field? I’m worried about strict JSON decoding in a couple codepaths.

2025-03-17 Michael Nguyen (author): Good call. The legacy decoder in `route_config_codec` is permissive (map-based) but I found one strict struct decode used in snapshots. Updated snapshots path to use the permissive decoder and added a regression test (old reader on new payload).
2025-03-18 Jordan Lee (review): For determinism, prefer reading the column only when it’s non-null AND passes validation. Otherwise fall back to legacy blob, not "default". Can you adjust?

2025-03-18 Michael Nguyen (author): Updated: dual-read now does (1) if column present and valid => use it, (2) else parse legacy blob, (3) else treat as default. Also emits `route_quant_profile_migration_read_fallback_total` with reason labels.
2025-03-18 Benji Okafor (review): Please document the exact rollout order for flags + backfill and what to check in dashboards. Support will ask.
2025-03-18 Michael Nguyen (author): Added a "Staged rollout plan" section to the PR body and a short internal note in `flags.yaml` descriptions. Also added metrics names + suggested queries.
2025-03-19 Connor O'Brien (review): Backfill needs a hard QPS cap and a safe stop mechanism. Also please confirm rollback steps are "disable dual_read" first.

2025-03-19 Michael Nguyen (author): Added token-bucket limiter (default 50 rows/sec, configurable) and a `--max-rows`/`--dry-run` option. Updated rollback section to disable dual_read first, then dual_write. Confirmed with SRE playbook expectations.
2025-03-20 Ethan Park (approve): Looks good. Thanks for catching the strict decode path.
2025-03-20 Jordan Lee (approve): Approved with the validation-first read behavior.
2025-03-20 Connor O'Brien (approve): Approved. Please coordinate enablement via release train thread.
